extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and humor theory; writers or critics seeking a conceptual account of comedic effect
extracted.subtask_description: A concise analytic framework for identifying and evaluating comic effects according to Schopenhauer: locating an abstract concept, a concrete particular, and a sudden perception of their incongruity. Useful for close reading, joke-writing diagnosis, or theoretical critique of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining formula: laughter = sudden perception of concept–object incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: "The cause of laughter in every case is simply the sudden perception of the incongruity between a concept and the real objects which have been thought through it in some relation, and laughter itself is just the expression of this incongruity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core criterion: identify the abstract concept invoked by the situation and the concrete object(s) thought through it; the comic arises when the audience suddenly perceives they do not fit together. Includes the corollary that the greater and more unexpected the incongruity, the stronger the laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species: Wit (Witz)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit occurs when we start with the concept and then suddenly find a particular case absurdly subsumed under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic signal: the setup foregrounds a general rule or classification; the punch or twist supplies a particular instance that exposes the absurdity of that subsumption. Emphasize surprise on the perceptual side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species: Folly / Absurdity (Narrheit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Folly arises when we start with the particular and then realize the concept under which the agent has acted does not really fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic signal: attention begins on a concrete character/action; the laugh comes when we recognize the agent is operating under a mismatched or ridiculous concept. Emphasize surprise on the conceptual side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive operation: Humorous bifurcation
rubrics_metrics.description: An idea believed to belong to one category turns out to belong to two (puns, double entendres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for semantic or categorical splits where a single sign/phrase maps to two categories simultaneously. Typical examples: wordplay, equivocation. Distinguish genuine perceptual/conceptual bifurcation from mere cleverness (see exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive operation: Humorous subsumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ideas thought distinct turn out to share a category (forced comparisons, 'how is X like Y' jokes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify cases where a particular is shoehorned under an inappropriate but technically possible concept, creating a forced likeness that yields comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: a genuine concept must be in play
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a rule, classification, or generalization governing expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comic requires an operative abstract standard or category against which particulars can be judged. If no conceptual expectation is invoked, no Schopenhauerian incongruity arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: a real particular must be presented
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific case with concrete features must be presented to be compared with the concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The particular should be vivid or determinate enough that its mismatch with the concept is appreciable; purely schematic or empty particulars will not produce the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: the particular must be paradoxically subsumed
rubrics_metrics.description: The particular does belong under the concept by some thread, but otherwise does not 'remotely belong there.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subsumption must be technically defensible (some logical or linguistic thread connects them) while evidently absurd on practical or perceptual grounds. This tension—partial fit plus obvious misfit—is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: recognition must be sudden
rubrics_metrics.description: The perception of the misfit must be sudden; gradual perception produces no laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is crucial: a 'click' or instantaneous reframing causes laughter. If the audience's realization is protracted or anticipatable, the Schopenhauerian comic effect is weakened or lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling rule: greater discrepancy → stronger laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater and more unexpected the incongruity, in the apprehension of the laugher, the more violent will be his laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a heuristic for evaluating punch strength: increase unexpectedness or widen the perceptual/conceptual gap to intensify the comic response (while preserving the tenuous thread of subsumption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive principle: comedy as perception's triumph over concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The comical is the perception's triumph over concept: reason's rigid categories are shown inadequate by the richness of particulars; laughter is intellectual revenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to frame interpretive readings: jokes expose limits of abstract thought and celebrate immediate perception. This principle helps explain why certain mismatches are funny rather than merely erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: pure word-games with no real subsumption are merely clever
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure word-games that lack genuine subsumption are clever but not funny under this account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between mere verbal cleverness (which plays on form without involving a concept–particular misfit) and true comic incongruity. If no substantive subsumption relation is at stake, treat as non-comical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: tragic mismatches that cause harm provoke pity, not laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where the concept's failure causes harm are tragic and elicit pity rather than laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the emotional valence of the mismatch: if consequences are harmful or elicit sympathy, they fall outside the comical even if an incongruity exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: unresolved misfits that never produce perception
rubrics_metrics.description: If the misfit is never perceived—i.e., the discrepancy never reaches a moment of recognition—no laughter occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the narrative or joke design includes a resolution moment where the audience can perceive the misfit; ambiguously unresolved situations do not satisfy Schopenhauer's account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist / questions for identifying Schopenhauerian comic
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of questions to determine whether an instance fits the framework: What concept is the setup invoking? What particular is being slipped under it? Does the particular technically fit while obviously not really fitting? Does the audience experience a sudden 'click' of perceiving the gap? Would tightening or loosening the concept ruin the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these questions sequentially when analyzing a joke or scene. The checklist operationalizes the necessary conditions and exclusions: positive answers indicate a Schopenhauerian comic, while negatives point to other humor mechanisms or mere cleverness.
